For whole-skin and dermis samples, the sample was cut into four equal size chunks and enzymatically digested using Miltenyi Whole Skin Dissociation (WSD) kit following manufacturer’s instructions with the exception that enzyme P was omitted to better preserve surface epitopes. Epidermis was digested using the Miltenyi WSD kit following manufacturer instructions with the same exception as above and only incubating 30 minutes at 37ºC.  Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from blood of patients with L-CTCL were isolated by density gradient centrifugation following manufacturers protocol (StemCell Technologies). In most cases, PBMCs were cryopreserved in RPMI-1640 media containing 30% human serum and 10% DMSO. Cryopreserved PBMCs were thawed in 37ºC water bath and washed twice in RPMI-1650 containing 10% human serum and allowed to recover overnight before setting up experiments.  Samples from multiple compartments (dermis, epidermis and blood) as well as multiple donors were multiplexed using cell hashing and stained with oligo-conjugated antibodies targeting surface antigens (for CITE-seq) before proceeding to fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS; for matched skin and blood samples) and subsequent single-cell segmentation using the 10X Chromium (Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 5’ reagent kit v2, 10X Genomics) following manufacturers instructions.

After cDNA synthesis, emulsion recovery and clean up following manufacturers instructions (Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 5’ reagent kit v2, 10X Genomics), full length cDNA was amplified by 13 cycles of PCR with addition of 25 nM of primers targeting the PCR handle present on all the hashtag oligo (HTO) antibodies (HTO_add: GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTGC*T*C) and antibody-derived tags (ADT; TotalSeq-C) antibodies (ADT_add: CTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAG*A*C) together with the cDNA primers included in the Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 5’ reagent kit v2 (10X Genomics). Following size selection, HTO and ADT sequencing libraries were constructed separately from the small cDNA fraction by 9 and 12 cycles of PCR using TruSeq/TruSeq and TruSeq/Nextera P5/P7 indexing primers, respectively. Gene expression (GEX) and TCRαβ sequencing libraries were constructed from the large cDNA fraction following manufacturer’s instructions. HTO, ADT, GEX and TCRαβ libraries were sequencing together on Illumina NovaSeq 6000 aiming to reach at least 4000, 10000, 25000, and 3000 paired-end reads per cell for the respective libraries.
data_processing: Sequencing reads from HTO and ADT libraries were counted using the Kallisto-KITE workflow [https://github.com/pachterlab/kite]. Sequencing reads from GEX and TCRαβ libraries were aligned and assembled using the CellRanger (v7.0.0) software. Ambient signal from GEX, ADT and HTO libraries was removed using CellBender (Fleming et al.). Initially cell barcodes having less than 100 genes detected or more than 50% of unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) derived from mitochondrial transcripts were removed. Further filtering was done following “overclustering” with scran::clusterCells clustering (NNGraphParam with k=5) and removal of clusters that consistently have low UMI counts, low number of genes detected and high fraction of UMIs derived from mitochondrial transcripts. Hashtagged cells were demultiplexed into their respective samples and cross-sample doublets were removed using the hashsolo function from the solo python library (Bernstein et al.). Some samples (primarily skin) were combined from multiple reaction wells (due to high cell numbers) during processing and each demultiplexed sample was exported as individual h5 files using DropletUtils::write10xCounts(type="HDF5") to make samples more accessible to the community.
